meta.title: EliteCadet SSB Academy — Day 2 Psychology Resource Catalogue
meta.scope: TAT, WAT, SRT, SD/SDT, and Full Day 2 (combined) preparation resources

inclusion_status_legend.recommended: Credible, substantive, safe to link and/or summarize — candidate for the platform
inclusion_status_legend.usable_secondary: Acceptable as a secondary/supplementary link but with a caveat noted in inclusion_notes
inclusion_status_legend.needs_verification: Could not be fully verified with available tools (e.g. JS-only content, second-hand app-store data, conflicting attribution) — a human should check before use
inclusion_status_legend.excluded_low_quality: Thin, templated/SEO-only, duplicate, or not actually test-specific — do not use
inclusion_status_legend.excluded_unverifiable: URL responds but no real content could be confirmed to exist there — do not link

notes_on_seed_sources.afpa.in: Credible private coaching academy (named retired-officer founder, DIPR-trained faculty, explicit no-guarantee disclaimer) but every Day 2 psychology page on the domain is a paid course, paid e-book, or paid video sale page. No free explanation, no free practice material, and no interactive/timed tool exists on the site itself.
notes_on_seed_sources.targetssb.in: A login-gated (Clerk auth) client-side single-page app. Every URL, including /read/TAT, /read/WAT, /read/SRT, /read/SD, returns HTTP 200 with an empty server-rendered shell — and the /read/ route was confirmed to be an unvalidated catch-all (a nonsense slug also returns 200), so a 200 response is not evidence real content exists there. No page content could be verified with available tools. Recommend excluding from the platform unless a follow-up pass with authenticated browser automation can confirm real content.

resources.title: What is Thematic Apperception Test (TAT) In SSB Interview
resources.short_original_description: Covers TAT's psychological origin, the 12-slide format (11 pictures + 1 blank slide, ~30s view / 3-4 min write), and names real psychometric scoring frameworks rather than sticking to generic tips.
resources.quality_notes: Above-average depth for a free explainer — cites named scoring frameworks (Miner Sentence Completion Scale, Defense Mechanisms Manual) instead of only listing generic advice.
resources.credibility_notes: Editorial-team authored (SSBCrack), not an individually credentialed expert, but SSBCrack is a long-established, widely-cited Indian defence-aspirant portal.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original article; safe to summarize in our own words, do not reproduce their story examples verbatim.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best free beginner TAT explainer found.

resources.title: TAT and PPDT Story Writing Tips
resources.short_original_description: Advises simple, natural language over 'impressive' vocabulary and stresses that a candidate's TAT story should stay consistent with their WAT/SRT/SD answers, since all four tests are read as one personality picture.
resources.quality_notes: Moderate depth — one worked example, general principles rather than a full narrative-structure framework.
resources.credibility_notes: SSBCrack editorial team, institutional not individual credibility.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original article; safe to link/summarize.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Good supplementary piece alongside T01; the cross-test-consistency point is genuinely useful and underexplained elsewhere.

resources.title: SSB Arena — Free TAT & PPDT Picture Practice with Timer
resources.short_original_description: A no-signup browser tool offering 30+ picture sets for PPDT and TAT practice under an enforced time limit, built by an independent developer with no coaching upsell.
resources.quality_notes: Genuinely interactive and completely free — the main strength is real timed practice, not theory. Picture provenance isn't disclosed, and there's no expert-authored guidance layered on top.
resources.credibility_notes: Individual hobby/community project (GitHub Pages); no institutional or named-expert backing. Credibility rests on functionality, not authorship.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Link to the tool; do not mirror or redistribute its images.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, functionality confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Fills the picture-practice-tool gap for TAT for free.

resources.title: TAT — Free Mock Series
resources.short_original_description: A free, automatically-timed TAT mock series (12 slides, 30s view / 4min write bell) run by a retired Army colonel as a free community SSB-prep project rather than a paid product.
resources.quality_notes: Timing accuracy matches the real format, and it is genuinely free rather than a lead-generation funnel — a meaningful differentiator from most coaching-site tools.
resources.credibility_notes: Run by a named, retired Indian Army officer (Col PP Vyas); the site cites past program participants recommended at SSB. Above-average individual-expert credibility for a free resource.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original mock content; link, do not scrape the picture sets.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, format and free-access confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: One of the strongest resources found across all categories — named credentialed operator + genuine free timed practice.

resources.title: Some Tips for Stories in TAT
resources.source_name: No Frills Academy (Col MM Nehru, Retd.)
resources.short_original_description: Specific TAT-writing rules — single-protagonist focus, realistic problem resolution, avoiding clichéd openings, sensible character/demographic matching — from a retired colonel who served as an SSB selector.
resources.quality_notes: Actionable and specific, though the underlying principles overlap with common SSB-coaching advice found elsewhere — not fully unique insight, but well-grounded.
resources.credibility_notes: Strongest individual-credibility signal among TAT articles: a named, retired Indian Army colonel with a stated SSB selector role (17 SSB Bangalore).
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original authored article; safe to link/summarize.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, author bio and content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best 'expert guidance' entry for TAT — genuine assessor-side experience.

resources.title: TAT Practice Pictures for SSB Interview
resources.short_original_description: Twelve practice images offered in a browse mode with model stories and a live-practice mode enforcing the real 30s/4min timing, filterable by theme (leadership, civic duty, family).
resources.quality_notes: Combines real timed practice with model-answer scaffolding and thematic filtering — more structured than a bare picture dump; access tier not stated on the page.
resources.credibility_notes: Established (since 2001) Delhi-based coaching institute stating retired SSB officer faculty (a Brigadier ex-IO, a Col ex-GTO, a Col ex-psychologist), though not individually attributed on this specific page.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Model stories are site's own content; link rather than reproduce.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Good secondary picture-practice option; verify free-vs-paid tier before linking prominently.

resources.title: How to Write Good TAT Stories for SSB — Complete Guide
resources.short_original_description: Lists common TAT errors and a four-part story structure recommendation.
resources.quality_notes: Templated/generic — repetitive bullet structure, heavy internal self-promotion links, no case studies or original research. Structurally near-identical to several other small coaching-site TAT articles found in this research pass (shared SEO genre, not independent content).
resources.credibility_notes: No author name or credentials disclosed beyond a physical address.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Not a verbatim scrape, but structurally derivative of a common template used across competitor sites.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed but low-value
resources.inclusion_notes: Adds nothing beyond T01/T05; representative of a large tier of thin coaching-site listicles found for this category — excluded rather than duplicated.

resources.title: WAT Word Association Test — Examples & Explanation
resources.short_original_description: Explains WAT as a test of spontaneous subconscious reaction rather than vocabulary, covers the 60-word/15-second format, and illustrates with the site's own example word-response pairs.
resources.quality_notes: Solid on mechanics and purpose; doesn't go into scoring theory. Examples appear to be the site's own creation, not a real official test bank.
resources.credibility_notes: SSBCrack editorial team — institutional credibility, not individually credentialed.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Safe to link/summarize; do not reproduce their example list as if it were our own.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best free beginner WAT explainer found.

resources.title: WAT — Free Mock Series
resources.short_original_description: Five separate free timed WAT mock sets (60 words, 15 seconds each) from the same free, retired-officer-led community SSB-prep project as the TAT mock series.
resources.quality_notes: Multiple distinct sets support repeated deliberate practice, which WAT specifically needs given the tight time pressure.
resources.credibility_notes: Same named retired officer (Col PP Vyas) as T04 — above-average credibility for a free tool.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original mock content; link, don't mirror word lists.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, format and free-access confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Pairs with T04 as the strongest free timed-practice source overall.

resources.title: WAT Words for SSB: Practice Words & Tips
resources.source_name: New Careers Academy (NCA Academy) — Hartaj Dhaliwal
resources.short_original_description: Pairs a handful of model-response word sets with roughly 100 additional grouped words for self-practice, alongside technique guidance on writing complete, spontaneous sentences.
resources.quality_notes: Above-average for a word-list article — separates 'model' sets from 'self-practice' sets to encourage active recall rather than passive reading.
resources.credibility_notes: Named author (Hartaj Dhaliwal, described as senior faculty and a retired defence officer at a coaching institute claiming a long operating history) — claim not independently verified beyond the site's own statement.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Free article promoting paid coaching, but the article content itself is not gated.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content and byline confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best practice-word-sets resource with real technique guidance attached.

resources.title: Word Association Test (WAT)
resources.source_name: How To Crack SSB — Ujjwal Chugh
resources.short_original_description: Do's-and-don'ts for WAT responses: personal unbookish phrasing, minimizing first-person pronouns, avoiding idioms/memorized phrases, short 4-5-word spontaneous sentences.
resources.quality_notes: Substantive tactical advice with a rationale behind each rule, though experience-based rather than research-cited.
resources.credibility_notes: Author is a selected NDA/SSB candidate (twice reached SSB stage) — a peer perspective, not a psychologist or ex-assessor; a lower credibility tier than T05 but still a genuine practitioner voice.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original article; safe to link/summarize.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content and authorship confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Good response-writing guidance; label clearly as candidate/peer perspective, not expert/assessor.

resources.title: WAT Complete Guide for SSB: Rules, Strategy & Real Examples
resources.short_original_description: Frames the 15-second constraint psychologically ('the psychologist wants your real sentence, not a good one'), gives four core response rules, and pairs good/bad examples across positive, negative and neutral words.
resources.quality_notes: Thoughtful psychological framing beyond mechanical tip-lists; references DIPR as a framework without independent citation. Links into the same site's WAT timed simulator (F01).
resources.credibility_notes: Unnamed 'editorial team' authorship — institutional-anonymous, comparable to SSBCrack's tier.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original content; safe to link/summarize.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Good bridge resource — pairs guidance with the platform's own timed tool (F01).

resources.title: WAT Practice — Timed with AI Analysis
resources.short_original_description: 60 timed words per session (15-second exposure) with automated AI feedback on the spontaneity/originality of written responses.
resources.quality_notes: The AI-scored feedback loop is a genuine differentiator from static timers, though the psychometric validity of the AI scoring is unverified and pricing could not be confirmed.
resources.credibility_notes: Self-described AI-powered defence-exam prep platform ('1000+ aspirants'); no ex-assessor/psychologist credential claimed.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original tool; link, don't reproduce word sets.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, feature claims confirmed, pricing unconfirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Interesting but verify pricing/access and AI-feedback quality before promoting heavily.

resources.title: Instructions for Situation Reaction Test (SRT)
resources.short_original_description: Explains SRT mechanics — 60 situations, 30 minutes, write in the answer booklet, respond with a first instinctive reaction rather than overthinking.
resources.quality_notes: Short but procedurally accurate; no fluff, no reproduced situations.
resources.credibility_notes: SSBCrack editorial team — institutional, widely cited in the community.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: General instructions only, no copyrighted situations reproduced.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best free beginner SRT format explainer found.

resources.title: 5 Easy Tips for Better SRT Responses
resources.short_original_description: Five response-writing principles — authenticity, concision, embedding Officer-Like Qualities, quality over quantity, avoiding copied phrasing — illustrated with a hypothetical (not real) example.
resources.quality_notes: Has a named author and gives actionable, non-generic principles rather than filler.
resources.credibility_notes: Byline: Gauri Agarwal, HR/Content Head at SSBCrackExams — a content professional, not a psychologist, on a known defence-prep publisher.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: No real SRT situations reproduced, only an illustrative made-up example.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best response-writing guidance found for SRT.

resources.title: Situation Reaction Test (SRT) in SSB
resources.short_original_description: Covers SRT format (60 situations/30 minutes), what a good response looks like, and behaviours to avoid such as heroic drama or incomplete solutions.
resources.quality_notes: Competent and accurate but follows a standard coaching-site template without distinctive original insight.
resources.credibility_notes: Institute claims 'Est. 2001' and retired-officer faculty, but the article itself has no individual byline.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: General guidance only, no reproduced test content.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Acceptable secondary explainer alongside S01.

resources.title: 10 Tricky Situation Reaction Test (SRT) Questions
resources.short_original_description: Walks through ten deliberately ambiguous or morally tricky situation categories (e.g. a bribe-seeking official) to illustrate where candidates typically misjudge the practical response.
resources.quality_notes: Useful for illustrating tricky situation categories; light on deeper analysis of why each one trips candidates up. Situations appear to be original framings, not real test items.
resources.credibility_notes: Brand-attributed (SSBCrackExams), no individual psychologist credited.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Illustrative original examples, not verbatim reproductions of real SSB booklet content.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Good common-mistakes companion to S01/S02.

resources.title: Self-Description Test (SDT): How to Write It Honestly & Effectively
resources.short_original_description: Explains the SDT's five-paragraph structure (parents, teachers/employers, friends, self, aspiration) within the 15-minute limit, and recommends gathering real feedback from people close to the candidate rather than inventing traits.
resources.quality_notes: Covers format plus a genuine self-reflection preparation method; no named author or distinguishing expertise markers beyond standard coaching-site guidance.
resources.credibility_notes: Published by a Kochi-based coaching institute; institutional rather than individually credentialed.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original guidance text, no reproduction of copyrighted SDT material.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best explanation + genuine self-reflection method found for SDT — closest thing to a real reflection exercise in the whole research pass.

resources.title: 20 SDT Templates to Practice for SSB Interview
resources.short_original_description: Worked SDT paragraph examples across all five categories, meant to model the shape and tone of a strong response.
resources.quality_notes: Useful as a structural model, but provides finished sample paragraphs rather than blank prompts — real risk that candidates memorize instead of genuinely self-reflecting.
resources.credibility_notes: Same publisher as D01; no individual author credited.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Site's own original composed samples, not reproductions of real candidates' sheets; safe to link, do not reproduce the sample text ourselves.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Link with an explicit 'these are models, not scripts to memorize' caveat on our own page — same warning AFPA's own e-book page states for its examples.

resources.title: What Is Self Description Test (SDT) in SSB?
resources.short_original_description: Explains SDT as the final psychological test, its five-paragraph/15-minute format, and the psychologist's rationale for cross-checking self-perception against the other three tests and the PIQ form.
resources.quality_notes: More substantive than bare format description — explains the strategic reasoning behind picking a correctable weakness and warns against contradicting the PIQ.
resources.credibility_notes: Brand-attributed (SSBCrackExams), no individual psychologist credited.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original explanatory text and illustrative, non-real sample content.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Good format explainer with a useful cross-test-consistency point.

resources.title: Self Description Test (SDT)
resources.source_name: How To Crack SSB — Ujjwal Chugh
resources.short_original_description: Candidate-perspective guide covering format/timing, advice to gather honest feedback rather than memorize a script, and common mistakes like contradicting other test answers or choosing an unbelievable weakness.
resources.quality_notes: Fairly thin on its own (basic guidance plus one example), but the named author's personal SSB attempt history is a distinct authenticity signal.
resources.credibility_notes: Author states he cleared NDA written exams and reached SSB stage twice — peer/practitioner experience, not formal psychology credentials.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Original text, no reproduction concerns.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Good common-mistakes companion to D01/D03.

resources.title: SSB Psychological Test Online Platform (PPDT/TAT/WAT/SRT/SD practice + Full Mock)
resources.short_original_description: A browser simulator displaying PPDT, TAT, WAT, SRT and SD prompts on strict SSB-pattern timings, including a 'Full Mock' mode that runs the entire Stage-2 sequence back to back; candidates write on paper and can get a PDF of the session.
resources.quality_notes: Genuinely interactive and timing-accurate (30s/4min TAT, ~15s/word WAT, 60 situations/30min SRT); core practice is free with an optional paid downloadable PDF pack — a legitimate freemium model.
resources.credibility_notes: Run by 'VKB Academy'; the site explicitly states it is not affiliated with the Armed Forces or DIPR — an honest independent tool, not falsely claiming official status.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Generates its own prompts rather than reproducing a known test set; safe to link.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, functionality confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Best full-Day-2 timed-simulation platform found; closest thing to a genuine continuous TAT→WAT→SRT→SD mock available for free.

resources.title: SSB Practice — Free PPDT/TAT/WAT/SRT/SD Simulator
resources.short_original_description: A no-signup browser simulator with dedicated modes per test (e.g. /tat, /wat?mode=strict), offering a non-pausable 'Strict Mode' for exam-realistic drilling and a pausable 'Practice Mode' for learning.
resources.quality_notes: Confirmed genuinely free with no registration; strong for realistic timed drilling of individual sections, though it does not appear to chain all four tests into one continuous session the way F01's Full Mock mode does.
resources.credibility_notes: No organizational/author information disclosed beyond a contact email — credibility rests on functionality, not named expertise.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Generates its own situations/words; no reproduction concerns.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly (root, /tat, and /wat?mode=strict), HTTP 200, functionality confirmed on each
resources.inclusion_notes: Complements F01 — use this for per-test drilling, F01 for the full combined mock.

resources.title: SSB Psych Test Simulator
resources.short_original_description: A free timer/simulator for TAT, PPDT, WAT and a custom stopwatch usable for SD/OIR practice, built as an independent side project.
resources.quality_notes: Functional and timing-accurate for the tests it covers, but a visibly small independent project rather than a maintained institutional product — treat as a lightweight supplement.
resources.credibility_notes: Named individual developer who explicitly discloses it is 'not an official SSB tool' — a positive transparency signal despite no coaching credential.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Self-built timer, no reproduced test content.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, functionality confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Fine as a third/backup timer option; F01/F02 are stronger primary picks.

resources.title: Live Psychology Test Practice — TAT, WAT, SRT, SDT (Real-Time Session)
resources.short_original_description: A livestreamed session from an established defence-coaching institute that walks viewers through timed TAT, WAT, SRT and SDT prompts in real time, functioning as a free video-led mock of the full Day 2 sequence.
resources.quality_notes: Rare among free resources in offering guided real-time practice across all four tests in one session. Page metadata (title, channel) was confirmed, but the actual on-screen video content/pacing could not be reviewed by automated fetch tools — a human should spot-check before featuring it prominently.
resources.credibility_notes: Major Kalshi Classes is a well-known, long-running (est. 2008, Allahabad) Indian defence-coaching institute reporting a large number of past selections and staffed by retired officers.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Institute's own produced YouTube content; safe to link, do not re-host, download, or transcribe substantial portions.
resources.verification_status: URL confirmed reachable and page metadata verified; full video content not reviewed by automated tools — treat as partially verified
resources.inclusion_notes: Best video resource found; note the partial-verification caveat before summarizing its content on our page — link and let students judge, don't claim specifics we haven't watched.

resources.title: Day 2 Psychology Test (overview of TAT, WAT, SRT, SD)
resources.short_original_description: A single-page overview of all four Day 2 tests with their individual timings and general approach principles for each.
resources.quality_notes: Good single-stop orientation for a first-time visitor to the Day 2 stage; explains approach principles without reproducing actual test stimuli.
resources.credibility_notes: SSBCrack editorial team — institutional, long-established.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Format description only, no proprietary content reproduced.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, content confirmed
resources.inclusion_notes: Ideal as the landing/orientation page for the whole Day 2 section before students branch into individual tests.

resources.title: Common Instructions for Interview at All SSBs
resources.short_original_description: The official candidate-instructions PDF published on the Indian Army's own recruitment domain, covering conduct expected at the SSB.
resources.quality_notes: Highest-authority document found in this research pass (official government/defence domain). Its internal text could not be extracted by automated fetch (compressed PDF stream), so its specific coverage of psychology-test detail is unconfirmed — recommend a human open and read it before we summarize any specifics from it.
resources.credibility_notes: Published directly on joinindianarmy.nic.in — the only genuinely official-tier source found across all four research passes.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Official government document; link directly, do not alter or misattribute its content.
resources.verification_status: URL resolves on official .nic.in domain and returns a valid PDF; internal text not machine-extractable — manual read recommended before citing specifics
resources.inclusion_notes: Use as a credibility anchor / 'straight from the source' link on the Day 2 landing page. Do not write summary claims about its contents until a human has actually opened and read it.

resources.title: Psych Test Mastery — SSB Psychological Test Coaching Program
resources.short_original_description: A paid service where a student completes TAT, WAT, SRT and SDT questionnaires under AFPA's instructions and receives a written personalized report plus a one-on-one feedback call from a retired-officer assessor.
resources.quality_notes: A structured sales funnel with testimonials and a money-back guarantee; it does not explain what the tests measure or how to answer them — no educational content for someone still learning the basics.
resources.credibility_notes: Cites DIPR-trained retired officers/GTOs as evaluators, consistent with AFPA's site-wide faculty claims.
resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Gated beyond the marketing copy; actual test material and feedback only released after payment.
resources.verification_status: Fetched directly, HTTP 200, confirmed as a sales page, not educational content
resources.inclusion_notes: Fine to list as one paid deep-evaluation option among several, clearly labeled paid; not a substitute for free explanatory content.

resources.title: Read Materials on TAT

resources.copyright_or_usage_notes: Unknown; likely requires login.
